question: What constitutes backbiting (ghibah), and when is it allowed?
answer:
Backbiting has been defined by the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ: to mention something about your brother, behind his back obviously, that he does not like to be mentioned. So this is a factual thing; what you have said is factual. You mention an awkward, an embarrassing issue, you mention something that will bring shame to that person and he doesn't want it to be known, and you mention it in front of other people: this is backbiting. You should not do that. As for lying, this is even worse, as our Prophet ﷺ said, and this is slander.

Now, when is backbiting allowed? Imam an-Nawawi mentioned six positions. Imam ash-Shawkani wrote a treatise, *Raf' al-Ribah fima Yajuz wa ma la Yajuz min al-Ghibah*, "Raising the doubt about what is and isn't allowed of ghibah." All of these treatises and tracts are really not comprehensive. They're simply trying to give you examples and illustrations of when you can do ghibah. And I'll give you some of these examples and exceptions, but realize these are exceptions. **The rule is you never do ghibah. That is the rule.** Do not think that every second thing you say will be an exception. Exceptions remain exceptions.

What are the exceptions? Number one, all of the fuqaha mentioned the number one exception:

> لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم

When zulm has been done to you, when somebody has taken your haqq, when somebody has lied, cheated, stolen your money, when somebody double-crossed you, you have the right to get your haqq back. You go to the people of authority, you go to the judge, you go to so-and-so, and you say, "What do I do? This person did this, I need help." So you're allowed to mention the faults of a person when your haqq has been taken.

Number two, some of our scholars mention when you're warning against a generic public evil. So this is a person whose presence is evil; he might be, for example, selling drugs to the children, whatever, you get my point. This is a person who has no sanctity. You need to warn the community: "This is a bad person. We don't want him coming to our community because of this." So a general maslahah, that you want to protect the community. Not a private sin. A person's private sins remain between him and Allah 'azza wa jall. Even if you see somebody drinking, it's none of your business to go and tell other people. But now suppose he's selling drugs to other people, he's selling drugs to the teenagers and kids. Now this is something else, and you need to now prevent that, even if it means mentioning what he is doing in public.

Another thing as well is if somebody comes to you for personal advice about a person that he wants to do business with, or he's interested in a marriage prospect, or any reason where it is a greater good that you mention. It is mentioned, from Fatimah bint Qays, and the hadith is in Bukhari, that she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Mu'awiyah proposed for me and Abu Jahm proposed for me. What should I do?" The Prophet ﷺ, in public, while Mu'awiyah was not there and Abu Jahm was not there, the Prophet ﷺ said, "As for Mu'awiyah, he has no money. You will not be successful marrying him. And as for Abu Jahm, he beats his wife. He will not be happy. Go and marry so-and-so."

So he mentioned faults about the other people, and they were not sitting there. What gives the right to mention faults? Now she's coming for what's called istisharah. Istisharah: specific advice. "I want to know about a business partnership. You know Fulan, Zaid, 'Amr? I want to enter a business partnership with him, and I know you had a business partnership." You will say, "Oh, I have to tell you, I found him to be somebody who double-crossed me multiple times. Beware." This is not ghibah. This is now istisharah; you're giving me advice to protect me. So this is something that is also allowed, insha'Allah ta'ala.

Now the gray area, and I'll just mention it, the gray area that our scholars have differed over in this regard, is very common. And again, not to be too generic or sexist, but this is a little bit more common in our sisters than brothers. We have our faults, and sometimes sisters have certain things as well that they're more prone to. The issue of talking about what happened to you with another person. So so-and-so did something to me; you're hurt; you want to tell somebody else what so-and-so did. You see the point here, right? Something happened to you. It's something dealing with you. We're not talking about brother X and brother Y doing something and now you're mentioning it; that's 100% ghibah. How about if brother X or sister X hurt sister Y? You are sister Y. Now you want to go and tell your husband, you want to go and tell other people, right? Is this ghibah or not? And this is, unfortunately, the common conversation that takes place in many households and many gatherings, of men and women as well.

And this is where Allah knows best. I would say we need to look very, very carefully: what is the niyyah behind mentioning this awkward conversation, behind mentioning what happened? If the niyyah is to name and shame, if the niyyah is to humiliate, then it is ghibah. But if the niyyah is to get advice: what should I do?

It's very common, for example, that a sister might say, "Oh, my husband did this and this, he said this and this." And she'll tell her best friend. She'll call up and say, "You know, my husband came home, he was in a bad mood, he did this and this." And she's basically expressing a frustration. Okay, now is it ghibah when the sister mentions what her husband did that's awkward, that's embarrassing? This is a very gray area, and Allah knows best.

What I will say is, and a brother can do the same as well, we need to look very carefully: what is the niyyah? If the niyyah is to bring about sulh, to bring about reconciliation. So the reason why the sister is telling her best friend is she wants to hear an opinion. She wants to hear, "What should I do? Was I in the right? Was he in the right? If I'm in the right, what can I do to get the situation back? If I'm in the wrong, should I apologize?" So if her niyyah is to bring sulh, then inshallah, if she goes to a trustworthy source, it is not ghibah. But if the niyyah is name and shame, if the niyyah is humiliate, then this would constitute ghibah. Because what's the purpose of telling the faults of another person, even if that has happened to you? And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best.
